source: AIDOC-catalogued Khmer farmer leaflet, "Coconut Cultivation Techniques for Farmers", prepared with NGO partners including Santi Sena, Buddhism for Development, and a farmer/agriculture association
text:
Backfilling the planting hole: after the dug hole has been left open for a period, before planting it should be backfilled with topsoil mixed with compost or manure; fertilizer is added at this stage so the seedling has a ready nutrient supply during its early, nutrient-demanding growth phase.

Selecting and setting the seedling: inspect and select a healthy nursery seedling that is not too old — the leaflet's illustration specifically shows a coconut seedling of about one year old being transplanted. Plant during a cool part of the day so the roots establish well without heat stress, and water immediately after planting to help the roots settle and establish quickly. The illustration shows a farmer carrying a bundled seedling to the field, seedlings being watered by hand with a watering can before planting, and one seedling shown soaking roots in a water container in preparation for transplanting.
